A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LCRON and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched across the layout changes and expanded appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original RecFlow experiments, ablations, streaming and sensitivity evaluations, and an industrial online A/B test.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds three-stage ranking, sorting-operator comparisons, training-parameter sensitivity, and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Equations 5, 11, and 12 add negative-label cross-entropy terms to v1's positive-only objectives. This substantially changes the documented supervision for both Le2e and Lsingle; v1 explicitly excluded negative-label supervision. Full-stage sampling, soft-sort normalization, and UWL remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use RecFlow Period 1 and industrial advertising data. Appendix C.2 adds coverage of rerank_neg and rerank_pos samples, using rerank_pos as ground truth for three-stage evaluation. This extends the evaluated selection task within the existing dataset and domain.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds standalone NeuralSort and SoftSort training as evaluated comparators. The main and industrial comparator rosters remain unchanged. ARF-v2's documented definition also inherits the revised Lsingle objective.

E3.justification: V2 adds three-stage DSSM/MLP/DIN evaluation, sorting-operator controls, four learning-rate/batch-size configurations, and GPU profiling. It explicitly sets training quotas to 10/10, whereas v1 identifies them with stage quotas of 30/20. This changes the reported setup without establishing whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing loss-removal, weight, streaming, and temperature analyses are retained. Appendices C–E add tests of sorter dependence, three-stage scalability, learning-rate/batch-size sensitivity, quota alignment, and computational costs, substantially broadening examination of robustness and practical behavior.

E5.justification: V1 reports five-run means, standard deviations, and t-tests for the ablation table only. V2 extends this reporting to the main comparison and three-stage experiment, and reports five-run means and standard deviations for sorting comparisons. These are newly documented practices, not evidence of an explicit increase in previously performed runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 updates baseline estimates, including FS-LambdaLoss joint Recall from 0.8674 to 0.8666, while LCRON's joint 0.8732 and industrial results remain. Single-stage metric assignments change: LCRON ranking Recall/NDCG becomes 0.8729/0.7291 instead of 0.7291/0.8729, so this is not evidence of performance improvement. New results include three-stage joint Recall of 0.7390, operator and training sensitivity, resource measurements, and quota-aligned Recall of 0.8714±0.0008.

T1.justification: Alongside the revised loss definitions, Appendix D adds asymptotic time and space analysis distinguishing O(DN) from O(DN²) costs. The central survival-probability bound and Appendix A derivation, including Equations 8 and 14–15, remain unchanged; no replacement bound proof accompanies the revised losses.

C1.justification: The central claims of recall-aligned joint training, stage collaboration, and improved public and industrial performance remain. The introduction changes the claimed advantage over ARF from avoiding gradient vanishing through normalization to fuller use of the soft permutation matrix.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive limitations concerning gradient conflicts, mismatched training and evaluation quotas, UWL's heuristic assumptions, and quadratic computational cost. V2 also restricts compatible sorting operators and revises explanations of ARF's shortcomings and bidirectional collaboration relative to ICC.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a LCRON-specific source-code link, baseline implementation provenance, TF-Ranking adaptation details, explicit hyperparameter search grids, and A800 runtime and memory information. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's existing architecture, optimizer, and online deployment descriptions.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused comparisons with FAA and SRCR, discusses optimal-transport sorting, revises ICC and ARF positioning, and connects future work to multi-task and meta-learning. The central positioning within joint cascade ranking remains. RecFlow's updated publication citation represents the same work.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative and much existing prose are retained, with localized rewriting of methodological explanations, related work, and conclusions. Appendix C gains subsections, and complexity, limitations, acknowledgements, and impact sections are added; the original narrative is not extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and relocating tables and figures. Six experimental tables are added. The existing temperature table moves from Table 6 to Table 8, while several main tables become much smaller column-width displays.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical support for its central claims: the main comparison gains uncertainty and significance reporting, and the previously asserted extension beyond two stages receives direct testing. Added robustness studies, implementation details, and explicit quota and loss-fusion limitations improve reproducibility and transparency. Some discussion remains inconsistent with the reassigned Recall/NDCG columns, and smaller tables impair readability, but these issues do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
